evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We support 85 primary health facilities in Ekiti State, Nigeria, to keep complete patient records. Behavior: each facility's record officer completes every outpatient record (date, diagnosis, treatment, age, sex) on the day of the visit. We interviewed 30 officers: 24 could not say how complete their own registers were, and most guessed 'about the same as everyone'. Registers and pens are in stock, and officers say time is not the problem. The state health information system gives us, for each facility and month, the share of outpatient visits with a complete record; the data are good except at three facilities with intermittent power. About 20 facilities are above 90%, 30 are between 60 and 75%, and the rest are below 50%. We want to send a monthly text to each record officer. The local government monitoring officer would also like to see the numbers. Design the report.
evals.expected_output: A feedback report specification in the output template with one metric, a comparison chosen by the rule, and separate content for facilities at the top and bottom.
assertions: The headline metric is the share of visits with a complete record at the officer's own facility.
States the comparison and the reason for it, and shows no rank or league table.
Says separately what facilities above 90% and facilities below 50% see.
Says what the monitoring officer may see or do with the figures.
Deals with the three facilities whose data are unreliable.
Requires results to be read separately for both ends and promises no effect size.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Our CHWs are underperforming. Design a feedback report for them.
evals.expected_output: The skill asks what shows that the health workers misjudge how they are doing, and what data exist for each of them, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks for the behavior and the evidence that not knowing, and not supplies, pay, or skill, is the barrier.
Asks what data exist for each health worker and how reliable they are.
Asks who else would see the report, or whether it could be used in appraisal.
Does not produce a feedback report specification.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: In our reading program in Bihar, teachers get a monthly SMS with the number of reading sessions the monitor recorded for them. In interviews most teachers guessed they ran the session 'most days' when the monitor's count was about half. The district education officer now wants the same monthly numbers sent to block education officers so they can 'act on it', and says they will be part of the annual teacher appraisal. The data come from two monitor visits a month. How should we set up the report?
evals.expected_output: The skill specifies the report to the teacher and says the appraisal use must not go ahead until a human-resources or labor specialist and program management have agreed written rules.
assertions: Specifies the teacher's report with the session count as the one metric.
Says a count from two visits a month is a thin basis for a personal number.
Names a human-resources or labor specialist, with program management, to agree rules of use before any pilot.
Says what to bring to them.
Does not design the appraisal use or present it as ready.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: We want to text every farmer in our program in Kaduna: '8 out of 10 farmers in your village have already planted the improved seed.' Nothing about the individual farmer's own planting. Can you design that feedback report?
evals.expected_output: The skill says a message about what most others do, with no figure about the person, is a social norm message and points to the skill for that.
assertions: Says the message carries no information about the farmer's own performance.
Does not produce a feedback report specification.
